No adopted exception for a following member-class template parameter was found.2395 records the fixed-length parameter-allocation ambiguity;2994 proposes an explicit exception for function templates and is OPEN, not a general adopted class-template permission. Thus the exact following-parameter source cannot impose a GCC/Clang-extension acceptance requirement under the current course contract. This does not justify rejecting a trailing expanded head: the valid trailing TT-head slice exposes a real f107 bug and is being repaired independently.

disposition.reason: This mixed TU contains B1 and insert1 UNUSED default TEMPLATE arguments sizeof(Args) with an unexpanded pack, explicitly within adopted CWG2746 no-valid-default rule. That is enough to remove whole-program mandatory requirements. Do not incorrectly extend this argument to B2/insert2 DEFAULT FUNCTION arguments: those can be bypassed by supplying the second argument, and their instantiation is demand-driven. Retain separate active-default and bypassed-default witnesses rather than claiming every function specialization is invalid.

disposition.reason: At the member-partial declaration, Vals occurs only in the dependent typename-specifier ValListWithTypes<ValTypes...>::WithVals<Vals...>. The nested-name-specifier is a nondeduced context, and14.8.2.5p6 makes the enclosing specified type nondeduced. Vals has no independently deducible occurrence, contrary to adopted1315. Instantiating the enclosing class creates the partial declaration; it does not add a new written deducible occurrence to its parameter pattern. The original only uses Impl<> and never demonstrates selecting the partial. A bounded actual-selection attempt also fails on GCC (selected member absent); that observation supports the distinction but is not the normative proof. A concrete nondependent Owner::List<N...> partial is a different declaration and passes all three, so retain it as an independent valid control. Drafting1755 addresses instantiation timing, not an adopted exception to1315.
